citation: John Lewis Krimmel, Black Sawyers Working in front of the Bank of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, 1811-ca. 1813. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 42.95.16.
author: John Lewis Krimmel
repository: The Metropolitan Museum of Art; object 12734 in the museum's collection API (isPublicDomain: true), image DT1805 at images.metmuseum.org.
locator: Open-access image DT1805: the four sawyers and the woman holding a child, foreground.
rights_note: The Met's Open Access images of public-domain works are released CC0. Proposed for use only as a reference picture the 1812 figures are judged against; nothing traced or sampled.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (dress research for the 1812 scene). Watercolour drawn in the war years. Black working men sawing cordwood in shirtsleeves: white shirts, one red shirt, striped and green waistcoats, blue and mustard trousers, black round hats, one white head-wrap; a Black woman in a head-wrap, white bodice or short gown and a pink-striped petticoat carries a small child in a white frock with an orange wrap.
note: Proposed for the 1812 dress reference sets; not a Chicago or Fort Dearborn record. Added for the 1812 women's dress (T-3464 dress build, tools/human_women_1812.py) from docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/dress.json.
what_it_supplies: working dress of free Black men and a woman in an American city 1811-1813, drawn at the time: shirtsleeves, waistcoats, round hats, head-wraps, short gown and striped petticoat, a child's frock
what_it_does_not_supply: the Old Northwest: this is Philadelphia
